la:noun:meatus.html:
mĕātus, ūs, m.
id.
,
a going, passing, motion, course (poet. and post-Aug.).
Lit.: solis lunaeque meatus,: caeli,: aquilae,flight,: spiritus,i. e. the breathing, respiration,: animae,

—

Transf., concr., a way, path, passage, : meatum vomiticnibus praeparare,: spirandi,: cur signa meatus Deseruere suos, left their paths, i. e. became darkened, eclipsed, : Danubius in Ponticum sex meatibus erumpit,discharges itself through six channels,; cf.: bifido meatu divisus Rhenus,divided into two channels,. —
The avenues of sensation in the body: homo septem meatus habet in capite, duos oculos, etc.,.
